newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks rebound, but still below 600 pts.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks rebound, but still below 600 pts.

text.p: A spurt of buying in late trade on Monday enabled Jakarta stocks to substantially recover from an eight percent plunge earlier in the day, brokers said.
They said investors bought back index heavyweights Telkom and Bank Negara Indonesia in the last hour of trade.
The composite index closed 2.93 percent, or 18.07 points, down at 599.64 points after plunging to an intra-day low of 565.78 points in the morning.
"The rebound was due to a spurt of buying in late trading," a senior analyst with a major local firm said.
"There was a rumour in the market that government pension funds and other foundations injected about three trillion rupiah to buy Telkom and BNI," he added.
In the broader market, losers led gainers by 137 to 22, with 24 counters unchanged. Total volume was about 716 billion rupiah.
Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) topped the active list with about 55 million shares traded, and was up 50 rupiah to 1,250 rupiah after touching an intra-day low of 1,000 rupiah earlier.
Telkom was last traded at 3,625 rupiah, up 175 rupiah on a volume of 10.6 million shares after plunging to 3,125 rupiah earlier.

"This morning there was panic selling, prompted by concern over fluctuations in the rupiah combined with market talk that international fund managers might downgrade their weighting on Hong Kong. If it is true, they will downgrade portfolios in the whole region," said Jordan Zulkarnain, a senior analyst with Pentasena Securities.

He attributed the small rebound at closing time to bargain-hunting. "The prices of some stocks are already irrational, lower than their booked value. Actually this is the best time to buy," Zulkarnaen added.
But he doubted the market would recover soon as there was no indication that the rupiah would stabilise.
"As long as the rupiah remain fluctuating, the stock market will remain speculative," he said.
A broker with Hong Kong-based securities firm predicted that sentiment will be weak on Tuesday. "Bargain-hunters will continue to buy but I don't think in any large amount," she added.
John Rahmat, an analyst with Schroders Indonesia recommended buys for ceramic manufacturer Mulia Industrindo and Semen Gresik, which in his opinion had touched rock-bottom prices.
Mulia fell on Monday to a year-low of 600 rupiah. It recovered to close down 75 rupiah at 750 on a volume of 9.7 million shares.
First-tier Bank International Indonesia was also active, closing 75 rupiah higher at 1,275 rupiah on a volume of 42 million shares on investor buy-backs.
